issues.failure_explanation: The paper fixes once and for all a 'bounded Lipschitz domain with polygonal boundary', which admits non-convex polygons/polyhedra. The theorem asserts the implication 'A in W^{1,\infty} implies \uast in H^2(D)' and, on that basis, the improved estimates with L^2-rate H^4 and energy rate H^6 (and their GPE analogues). For a polygon with a re-entrant corner (e.g. an L-shaped domain) and A = I, V smooth and nonnegative, the principal eigenfunction has a corner singularity of type r^{\pi/\omega} with \omega > \pi, which is not in H^2; hence the premise A in W^{1,\infty} does not yield \uast \in H^2 under the paper's standing hypotheses, and the improved estimates (H^4 / H^6, equivalently O(H^3) in H^1 and O(H^4) in L^2) are not established in the stated generality. The claimed regularity requires an additional hypothesis on the domain (e.g., convexity), which the source does not impose.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard hypothesis that the domain is convex (or otherwise of class C^{1,1}) in the Lipschitz-A case of both theorems, or restate the implication as an explicit assumption '\uast \in H^2(\D)'; the statements, their proofs by citation, and the rough-coefficient estimates remain unchanged otherwise.
issues.overall_effect: The improved estimates (L2-error O(H^4), energy error O(H^3), energy/eigenvalue error O(H^6)) claimed in Theorem theorem:LOD-estimates-linear-setting and, identically, in Theorem theorem:LOD-estimates-GPE are not established for the full class of domains allowed by the paper's standing assumptions; for non-convex polygonal domains with Lipschitz coefficients the improved rates are unsupported (only the rough-coefficient estimates of the first part remain justified). The related prose discussion of the O(H^3)/O(H^4)/O(H^6) superconvergence for smooth A inherits the same gap.
issues.title: Claimed H^2-regularity of the minimizer does not follow from the paper's standing hypotheses
issues.why_classification: A standard local hypothesis (convexity of the polygonal domain, or directly assuming \uast in H^2) restores both statements without any new argument, construction, or weakening of the paper's central rough-coefficient rates; only the secondary smooth-coefficient regime loses non-convex polygonal domains, so the method, its main rates, and its advertised scope all survive.
